$comment: GOLDEN VECTORS — decisions/0026's conformance suite, finally existing.
0026 said, in the present tense, 'Every platform runs the same vectors; any platform failing any
vector fails CI'. No vectors existed. This file is the first of them, and it starts here because
iOS reported the concrete gap: their decisions/0027 fallback case HAS NEVER EXECUTED. No server
has ever sent an unrecognised enum, so `.unrecognised` decoding, `.rawValue` on it, and the
`gameLabel(game.rawValue) ?? "Pokémon"` fallback are all unexercised — and that last one would
These vectors need no server change and no ninth game to exist. That is the point: the failure
is reachable from a fixture today, and every platform can be made to face it now rather than
on the morning a ninth game ships.
THE ASSERTION IS ROUND-TRIP EQUALITY, chosen because it is the same check in three languages
with no path DSL and no per-language expectation table. Decode the payload, re-encode it, and
compare. One assertion proves three things at once: it decoded rather than threw (0027 item 1),
the unrecognised value survived rather than being dropped (item 2a), and nothing else in the
object was lost on the way.
EVERY VECTOR DECODES THROUGH ITS CONTAINING RESPONSE TYPE, never the enum alone. The failure
being guarded is a decode error PROPAGATING from a field to the whole object; a fixture that
decoded the enum directly would pass and prove nothing about the path that actually breaks.

vectors.name: ninth_game_in_catalogue_lookup
vectors.why: A game this build has never heard of. The scenario 0027 was written for, and the one that would label a ninth game 'Pokémon' on iOS.

vectors.name: ninth_game_in_one_candidate_only
vectors.why: The shape that bites hardest: a list where most entries are fine. A propagating throw loses the GOOD candidates too, so the picker shows nothing rather than showing fewer.

vectors.name: unknown_confidence_in_catalogue_lookup
vectors.why: Not just GameId — 0027 item 4 covers EVERY generated enum, and confidence is one. Picked deliberately over a made-up field: an unrecognised value has to be exercised on a real enum, or the vector proves nothing about the generated code.
